turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Driving sounds like it saved you some stress this morning, and that iced espresso drink is a great way to start the day. Did you listen to anything interesting on your commute?

turns.text: I actually did! I finally started that real-life murder investigation podcast my coworker recommended a while back. It's so suspenseful, I was almost disappointed when I pulled into the clinic parking lot!

turns.text: Oh, the true-crime one! I'm glad it lived up to the recommendation. It's always great when a commute goes by quickly like that. Are you getting a decent break for lunch today?

turns.text: Yes, I'm actually on my break right now. I brought a homemade bowl filled with seasoned rice, beans, salsa, and peppers that I threw together at home. It's a nice, fresh burrito bowl style lunch.

turns.text: That sounds delicious and satisfying for a busy shift. How are things going outside of work? Have you and Tom had any time to think more about the summer wedding plans?

turns.text: We actually spent some time last night looking at local caterers. It's a lot of work, but we're starting to get a better picture of what we want. Tom has been super helpful with sorting through all the options.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: It's wonderful that you two are tackling it together. Are you still finding some downtime for your sourdough baking, or has the wedding planning taken over your evenings?

turns.text: It's definitely a balancing act! I haven't baked a loaf this week, but I did feed my starter yesterday. Dash was sitting right by my feet the whole time, hoping I'd drop something.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Dash is always on kitchen duty, just in case! How is your ankle feeling lately, by the way? Is it completely back to normal after that sprain?

turns.text: Oh, it's completely healed up now, thanks for asking. I'm totally back to my normal routine and don't feel any pain at all.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's fantastic news. I'm glad you're fully recovered. Well, I'll let you get back to your lunch and the rest of your shift. Talk to you later!
